title: Building a rink hockey management game with AI — early experiments from someone who doesn’t know how to code
author: FerjorPT
selftext:
Hi everyone! I’m Fernando, I’m 51 and I’m from Portugal.

I’ve been working on a personal project called Rink Hockey Manager (RHM), a management game dedicated to rink hockey — the sport played on quad skates, rather than ice or inline skates.The ambition is to explore tactics, player development and club management around a sport I care about. 

I want to be honest about my starting point: I don’t know how to code. I use ChatGPT and Codex to help turn my ideas into experiments. I’ve even nicknamed them Gip and Sol. Giving them names hasn’t stopped them from producing bugs! 😅

My part is defining what I want, explaining the sporting behaviour, setting priorities, testing the results and deciding what needs to change. One thing I’m learning is that describing the intended behaviour and getting a simulation to reproduce it reliably are very different challenges.

In one of our tests, almost everyone gathered behind the same goal instead of playing hockey. We decided they were having a barbecue. Apparently, nobody had told the goalkeeper he was hosting! 😅

https://i.redd.it/z07swvbvaaxh1.png

We now have a small “Laughing with Bugs” section on the website. These moments are funny, but they also show how difficult it is to get player movement right. I mean, i know what i want but Gip and Sol... well they were on the barbecue aswell 😂 Seriously, the players need to make decisions that make sense within the sport, and we’re still working towards that.

RHM is at a very early, experimental stage. There is no public playable demo, and the match engine hasn’t been validated yet. Some of the material on the website is conceptual. I have no release date, and I can’t promise that I’ll finish it. It´s a dream that i am trying to fullfill.

I launched the website to share the journey and start listening to people, both those who already know the sport and those discovering it for the first time.

For others working with AI on simulations: how do you test whether agent behaviour is actually correct, rather than just looking convincing? I’d be interested in hearing about small, repeatable tests that have helped you catch problems.

The website is available in six languages: Portuguese (Portugal), Portuguese (Brazil), English, Spanish, French and German. You can choose your language from the menu.

Here’s the project, if you’d like some context:  
[https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/](https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/)

Thank you so much for reading!  
Fernando
